summary:
[  edit  ]
The  Group   SOP  generates groups of points or primitives according to various criteria and allows you to act upon these groups. Elements can occur in more than one group. Groups are used in many parts of the  SOP  Editor to specify which portion(s) of input geometry you wish a  SOP  to act upon.
You can also create ordered groups. To do so, check the Ordered button.

parameters.label: Group  Name
parameters.name: crname
parameters.description: The name of the group to be created. The default name is set to match the name of the  SOP .

parameters.label: Entity
parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: ⊞  - Primitives or Points.

parameters.label: Geometry Type
parameters.name: geotype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the geometry type group. The selection will only pertain to the geometry type specified. e.g. If you only wanted to group polygons.

parameters.label: All Types
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: All geometry will be selected.

parameters.label: Use Number
parameters.name: usenumber
parameters.description: Allows selection of grouping of entities by number. When the Enable button is Active, the selection options become active and can be used to select entities. The fields available are listed below.

parameters.label: Create Ordered
parameters.name: ordered
parameters.description: When selected, elements in the group are traversed in the order they are selected; otherwise they are traversed in creation order.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.name: groupop
parameters.description: ⊞  - When the Number Enable button is checked, this option groups entities based on a defined Pattern or by a Range.

parameters.label: Group  by Pattern
parameters.name: grppattern
parameters.description: Select a pattern in the Pattern field below.

parameters.label: Group  by Range
parameters.name: grprange

parameters.label: Group  by  Expression
parameters.name: grpexpression
parameters.description: Select a range using the Filter  Expression  field below.

parameters.label: Pattern
parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Activated when Operation is set to  Group  by Pattern. In this field, enter the range of primitives to select. The required syntax is "S.P", where S is the index of the parent surface, and P the profile index on that surface. You can mix primitives with profiles in the list. A mixed group is automatically ordered.
6  selects six profiles on primitive 0,

parameters.label: Transfer Selection to Pattern
parameters.name: transfer
parameters.description: This allows you to define the range of points / primitives visually by selecting them in the Viewport with the Select state. Clicking this button transfers the selected points/primitives into the Pattern field as a compacted range (e.g.  1-23 40 67-100 ). This eliminates the need for typing the point or primitive numbers manually.

parameters.label: Note:  Point and primitive selections can be dumped directly into  Group  fields without use of the  Group   SOP . Do this by selecting the points or primitives in the Viewport with the Select state. Then the pop
parameters.description: up N menu beside the  Group  field of the  SOP  you want to cook should display the selection in the input  SOP  (e.g. "grid1's  Primitive  Selection"). Ranges are automatically compacted.

parameters.label: Start / End
parameters.name: range
parameters.description: ⊞  - Activated when Operation is set to  Group  by Range. Select the start and end of the primitive/point number selection.

parameters.label: Select _ of _
parameters.name: select
parameters.description: ⊞  - Activated when Operation is set to  Group  by Range. Select every nth occurrence of every mth entity in the above Start/End range.

parameters.label: Filter  Expression
parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: The Filter  Expression  provided is evaluated for every point/primitive. Wherever it is true, the entity is added. All the local variables of point and primitive are present, though only accessable when the right type of group is being created.

parameters.label: Use Bounds
parameters.name: usebounds
parameters.description: This option is used for selecting entities based on bounding volumes: Bounding Box, or Bounding Sphere. When Active, the selection options become active and can be used to select entities. The fields available are listed below. The bounding volume can be seen in the viewport as guide geometry.

parameters.label: Bounding Type
parameters.name: boundtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects the type of bounding volume to use

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.name: usebbox
parameters.description: Entities contained within the box are selected.

parameters.label: Bounding Sphere
parameters.name: usebsphere
parameters.description: Entities contained within the sphere are selected.

parameters.label: Bounding Object (points only)
parameters.name: usebobject
parameters.description: Points contained within the Object are selected. Make sure the object consists of well formed polygons. If using an irregular mesh, convert to polygons with a Convert  SOP , then use a Divide  SOP  to convex sides to 3.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.name: size
parameters.description: ⊞  - Dimensions of either the Bounding Box or Bounding Sphere in X, Y and Z.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - The X, Y, and Z coordinates of the center of the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Use Normal
parameters.name: usenormal
parameters.description: This option is used for selecting entities based on the angle of the entity normals. When the Active, the selection options become active and can be used to select entities. The fields available are listed below.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: ⊞  - The default values of 0, 1, 0 create a normal vector straight up in Y, which is perpendicular to the XZ plane, which becomes the primary axis. The 1, 0, 0 points the normal in positive X, giving a normal axis perpendicular to the YZ. The plane may be positioned at an angle by using values typed in (1, 1, 0 gives a 45 angle plane) or interactively by using the direction vector jack. Values between 0 and 1 should be used.

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: The value entered in this field generates an angle of deviation from the primary axis. This can be visualized as a cone where the radius of the base of the cone is defined by the Spread Angle and the axis of the cone is determined by the Direction axis. Viewing the primitive normals in the viewport, you can see that any primitives with normals that have an angle that lies in the range of angles defined by the cone will be selected and grouped.

parameters.label: Backface from
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: This menu allows you to select an object. Typically, a camera object would be chosen. The primitives which are backface when viewed from the object specified will be grouped or selected.

parameters.label: Use Edges

parameters.label: Edge Angle

parameters.label: Edge Depth

parameters.label: Edge Depth
parameters.name: edgestep
parameters.description: Enter the depth of the edge (only for point groups).

parameters.label: Point Number

parameters.label: Unshared Edges
parameters.name: unshared
parameters.description: When selecting points, this option selects the points of a ploygonal mesh which appear on the boundary (i.e. those which are not shared) for inclusion in the group, and orders them. In addition to polygonal meshes, this option also finds the boundaries of geo Hulls and open faces.

parameters.label: Create Boundary Groups
parameters.name: boundarygroups
parameters.description: When selecting points with the Unshared Edges parameter, this option becomes available. Enabling it creates new groups of the form: <name>__< n> , (two underscores) where the < name> is the  Group  Name specified in the Create page. Numbers < n> begin at zero, and increment as more groups are created.

parameters.label: These groups contain the points on each boundary of the surface. For example, if you have a grid with a hole in the middle of it, two new point groups are created
parameters.description: one containing the points for the outer boundary and one with the points from the hole. These new point groups are also ordered.

* **Características clave:** * Utiliza atributos de detalle `pCaptPath` (rutas a los componentes que actúan como huesos) y `pCaptData` (matrices de "bind/rest pose"). * Usa el atributo de punto/vértice `pCapt[]` que contiene pares de índice de transformación y peso. * Puede realizar deformaciones en la **CPU** (usando `Deform SOP`) o en la **GPU** para mayor velocidad. * Para la deformación en GPU, la geometría puede necesitar ser dividida en "Bone Groups" si hay muchos huesos. * **Uso simple:** Para animar personajes o modelos 3D que tienen un esqueleto, permitiendo que la malla se deforme de manera realista a medida que los huesos se mueven. * **Skin POP (POP de Superficie)** * **Función principal:** Conecta arreglos de datos en 2D (o más) para formar una **malla de triángulos o cuadrados**. * **Características clave:** * Por ejemplo, puede tomar varias "line strips" y unirlas para formar una superficie.

* **Métodos de eliminación:** * **Por atributo (`Attribute Page`)**: Elimina basado en los valores de los atributos de puntos o primitivas. Puedes combinar lógicas como "P(0) > 0 Y P(1) < 0" para eliminar puntos en una sección específica del espacio. * **"Thin" (`Thin Page`)**: Elimina basado en rangos definidos por parámetros, pasos o aleatoriamente. * **Por patrón (`Pattern Page`)**: Elimina basado en la coincidencia de patrones. * **Por grupo (`Group Page`)**: Elimina basado en si los puntos o primitivas pertenecen a ciertos grupos. * **Por límites (`Bounding Page`)**: Elimina basado en rangos delimitadores de cualquier atributo. * Cuando eliminas primitivas, los puntos o vértices que ya no se usan también se eliminan automáticamente. * Cuando eliminas puntos, los vértices y primitivas que los usan pueden ser eliminados parcial o totalmente. Workshop Plan ### Objective Equip participants with a solid understanding of POPs, their advantages, and practical use in TouchDesigner projects. ### Duration 2-3 hours, split into theory and hands-on segments. ### Structure #### Part 1: Introduction (30-45 minutes) - **What are POPs?** (10 min) - Definition, purpose, GPU benefits. - **POPs vs. SOPs** (15 min) - Key differences, when to use each. - **Core Concepts** (15 min) - Points, primitives, attributes, groups. #### Part 2: Hands-On Demos (1.5-2 hours) - **Demo 1: Basic POP Workflow** (30 min) - Create a `Point Generator POP`, add `P` and `Color` attributes, render with a `Render TOP`. - **Demo 2: Attribute Manipulation** (30 min) - Use `Math POP` to modify `P`, create a custom attribute, and swizzle components. - **Demo 3: Particles and Point Clouds** (30 min) - Build a simple particle system with `Particle POP` and a point cloud with `Point File In POP`. - **Demo 4: Integration** (30 min)
